## Grammar

Basic word order is SVO; it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; demonstrative before the noun; numeral order varies; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has no definite article, no indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, nominative-accusative alignment, singular, dual and plural, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past and perfective; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator after the verb; yes/no questions use intonation alone. Verbs do not agree with their arguments.
Other features: alienable and inalienable possession told apart; verb reduplication; adjectives that behave like verbs; a periphrastic causative; no passive; question words moved to the front; a decimal counting base; a 'have' verb for possession.
Measured morphology: 9 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 0.0 (0 free word … 3 fused), 0 paradigm cells, 0 of them with allomorphy.

### Families a speaker feels

The roots a speaker still feels: a derivation or compound younger than 3 kyr whose parts are still in use (per-word `roots`). 3 families of 3+ words; 12% of the 701 words share a root with another word.

The largest: **country** *li˨ŋo˦ŋ* (N, coined 20 kyr ago in the white dragon proto-language); 4 words have it as their main root, 4 contain it.

## Sample sentences

Built from this language's own words, word order, markers and agreement (planet/language/sentences.py). Each has the form line (‘-’ an affix boundary, ‘=’ a clitic boundary), a morpheme-by-morpheme gloss, the free translation, then the whole sentence in IPA (after the simple joining rules: a glide between two vowels, a nasal taking the place of a following stop) and in the book spelling. Nothing here is attested speech; it is what the grammar data implies.
